title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 420–427 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on two generators. ρ is an order-3 automorphism cyclically permuting the three punctures. σ_∞ is an involution attached to ∞. l_1 is a loop (inertia) generator. φ̂ is a fixed automorphism. On this page φ̂ enters only through the commutation condition and the second relation (30).

Groups involved:
- M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3}, with quotient N_{0,3}^{!~}.
- M^{!≈} is the subgroup of automorphisms that 'ultimately commute' with φ̂.
- On the previous page Grothendieck gets a split extension 1→Π̂_{0,3}→M^{!≈}→N^{!≈}→1. The section M^{!≈}(0)≅N^{!≈} consists of the normalized automorphisms u_g.
- Every element of M^{!≈} is written uniquely as int(f^{-1})∘u_g. This is how the normalized triples (α,β,f) of 'cor. 1' are to be read: g = α ρ(α)^{-1} and g l_1^{-ν} = β σ_∞(β)^{-1}.

This page: a summary ('Récapitulation'/'Résolution') of what that gives.

(i) N^{!~} ≅ M^{!~}(0) is in bijection with the ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} satisfying:
- (30a) ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1;
- (30b) ξ = (φ̂(ξ) σ_∞(φ̂(ξ))^{-1}) l_1^ν, for a suitable ν ∈ Z.

(ii) Equivalently, put ξ = α ρ(α)^{-1} with α in an enlarged group Π̂_{0,3}^~. Then (30a) holds automatically, since ρ³ = id makes the product telescope to α ρ³(α)^{-1} = 1. One only has to impose (30b) on α ρ(α)^{-1}. This is the nonabelian 'Hilbert 90' trivialization: a ρ-norm-one element is a ρ-coboundary. Its justification is that an element ξρ of order 3 in Π̂ ⋊ Z/3 is conjugate to ρ.

(iii) The automorphism attached to ξ is given by the formulas (18): u_ξ(σ_∞) = (ξ l_1^{-ν}) σ_∞ and u_ξ(ρ) = ξ ρ. These are the images of the two torsion generators of the orbifold group. It is a 'normalized' automorphism, in the style of the GT action on x and y.

(iv) Composition: u_{ξ'} u_ξ = u_{ξ''}. Grothendieck refers to p. 395' (52), and the next page gives ξ'' = u_{ξ'}(ξ)·ξ'. This is the twisted (crossed-homomorphism) group law, exactly analogous to the multiplication law of GT^, f∘f' = f(f'(x,y) x^{λ'} f'^{-1}, y^{λ'})·f'.

Purpose: an explicit 'equation des lacets' description of the stabilizer-type subgroup of the Teichmüller-tower automorphism group in genus 0 with three points. It has a 3-cycle relation (the analogue of Drinfeld's hexagon) and a 2-cycle/σ_∞ relation twisted by φ̂ and by a power of l_1. Grothendieck then extends it by S_3, giving (34)–(37) on the next page.
errors: The deleted computation at the bottom attempts ξ'' = α''ρ(α'')^{-1} with α'' = u_{ξ'}(α)·α'. As written it is garbled; the leading α'' should not appear. Grothendieck crossed it out and replaced it with (33) on the next page.

Grothendieck tacitly assumes the bijection ξ ↔ α (ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}). This needs the conjugacy of order-3 elements in the profinite completion of the orbifold group. The fact is true (Z/2*Z/3 is good / torsion is conjugate to finite subgroups), but it is not argued here. α is also only determined up to ρ-invariants, which explains the passage to the enlarged group Π̂^~.

ideas.what: Parametrizing automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} normalized on the torsion generators ρ, σ_∞ by an element ξ satisfying a 3-cycle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 and an involution relation, with a twisted group law ξ''=u_{ξ'}(ξ)ξ'
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld's hexagon/2-cycle relations) and its composition law
ideas.where_published: Programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this explicit form is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Trivializing the 3-cycle (norm) relation via ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} (nonabelian H^1(Z/3, Π̂) trivial, via conjugacy of profinite torsion)
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian coboundary parametrization; conjugacy of finite-order elements in profinite completions of virtually free groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Serre's trees / goodness of PSL2(Z)); used in GT literature (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)

ideas.what: Split extension of the automorphism group by inner automorphisms, with a canonical section of normalized automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Aut = Inn ⋊ normalized automorphisms (Out lifted via normalization)

missed.claim: This is an independent, pre-Drinfeld-style derivation in Grothendieck's notes of a GT-type group in the (0,3) case. It uses a 3-cycle relation, a σ_∞-relation twisted by an automorphism φ̂ and a power l_1^ν, and the crossed group law. The φ̂-twisted second relation (an 'ultimately commuting with φ̂' subgroup) does not correspond to a standard variant in the GT literature that I know of. It would be worth comparing with the Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura variants.
missed.quote: ξ=(φ̂(ξ) σ_∞(φ̂(ξ))^{-1}) l_1^ν pour ν∈Z conv.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical documentation of Grothendieck's own route to GT-type relations. A φ̂-twisted subgroup might match a known relative or arithmetic version of GT, or define a new one.

deep.surprise_reason: A summary page of a computation whose structure (3-cycle relation, twisted composition law) is close to the now-standard GT^ formalism. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own version, but the mathematics is largely routine relative to the known theory. The φ̂-twist is the only unclear, possibly nonstandard ingredient.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion read as '(Micro-probabilisation)' is more plausibly '(Récapitulation)'. The underlined word read as 'Résolution' may itself be 'Récapitulation'; uncertain.
'Π̂_{0,3}^{~}' in the 'posant ξ=α.ρ(α)^{-1}' line has a hat over the tilde, written π_{0,3}^{~^}.
Formula (30), first line: ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 is confirmed by the image.
In (32) the image reads u_{ξ'}u_ξ = u_{ξ''}, consistent with the transcription.
